Map the user objective, period, entities, exclusions, and evidence permissions before selecting any research action.
Split the information need into independent domain questions and choose sources spanning primary evidence and meaningful competing explanations.
Retrieve and inventory diverse relevant material once; preserve original URLs, timestamps and document fingerprints with provenance.
Investigate each domain through focused search questions; distinguish source statements, estimates, assumptions and unsupported conclusions.
Cross-check source claims, revisions, dates, units, opposing evidence and gaps. Request deeper source retrieval only when expected information gain merits it.
Produce precise source-attributed evidence packs for dependent specialists, separating verified claims from provider attribution and unknowns.
